title: Three things each morning
header_line: My analysis of one book on habits. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What are your top three things to remember each morning?

I asked what three things you would think about each morning so that you do not fall for the wrong temptation, such as the wrong client. A student answered: start with gratitude, stick to your values by setting goals that align with them, and set priorities, the actionable items for today.

I said that I ask: are these my values? I said I would rather read a good book and spend time with close friends, and that this makes me more careful. I said I was not saying one set of values is better than another.
I said that being present and grateful stops you getting contaminated by the fabricated world of I need this and I need that.

A student asked how to use temptation bundling, in which the book says you pair something you want with something you need, to associate something with gratitude. Another said: you are just setting anchors.

A student offered: bundle a cup of coffee with journaling what you are grateful for. If you anchor it to pleasure often enough, it becomes unconscious, and eventually the journaling stays associated with the pleasure.

I asked how gratitude could be bundled with a goal such as growing a business. A student said: if you are grateful for the relationships and systems you have, you will be more conscious of ways to improve them, instead of thinking you need more capital.
What will you bundle with something you already enjoy?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write three things you are grateful for.
Write the goal that fits your values.
Write something you enjoy that you will bundle with a need.
Write how you will check that it is your value, not a fabricated one.

check.q: What was the first morning thing a student chose?
What did a student say about bundling coffee with journaling?
What did I say being grateful stops?
choices: Getting contaminated by the fabricated world

recap: Start with gratitude, values and priorities. Bundle the good.
